title: Northwind customer onboarding
summary: Northwind Onboarding is the tool the team uses to set up a new customer. An Onboarding Officer first searches for the customer by postcode and surname so that no duplicate record is created. If the customer is new, the officer enters their details, uploads a photo of an identity document and submits the record for approval, at which point it locks. A Team Lead approves the record from the Approval Queue. The system then shows a Confirmation screen with a customer reference number, which the officer gives to the customer, and sends a welcome email to the address entered.
actors: Document checker (role not identified by the expert)

actions.description: Enters postcode and surname and presses Search; matching existing customers are listed below on the same screen
Presses Clear to empty the search fields
Presses Open on a result row to open an existing customer (not shown in the recording)
Presses Create new customer when the customer is not found
Picks the Account type (Personal or Business) from the dropdown
Ticks 'Customer has given marketing consent' only if the customer said yes
Presses Save and continue after filling in the details
Presses Choose File to pick the ID document image or PDF
Picks the Document type from the dropdown
Presses Upload; the document appears in the Uploaded documents table with status Pending check

Presses Submit for approval; the record is locked for editing (the next screen shown in the recording was the Approval Queue, but the submit itself was not shown, so where the officer lands is unconfirmed)
Team Lead presses Approve on a row with status Awaiting approval (button only shown to the Team Lead role; the press itself was not shown, so the screen that follows is unconfirmed)
Presses Start another customer (not shown in the recording)
Presses Print confirmation (not shown in the recording)

journey.description: The Onboarding Officer enters the customer's postcode and surname and presses Search to see whether the customer already exists.
When the customer is not in the results, the Onboarding Officer presses Create new customer.

The Onboarding Officer fills in the mandatory details (First name, Last name, Date of birth, Account type, Postcode), any optional contact and address details and the marketing consent tick, then presses Save and continue.
The Onboarding Officer chooses a photo of the customer's ID, picks the Document type, presses Upload so the document sits in the table as Pending check, then presses Continue to review.
The Onboarding Officer reads through the summary of everything entered and presses Submit for approval, after which the record is locked for editing.
The submitted customer sits in the Approval Queue with status Awaiting approval and an assignee, and a Team Lead presses Approve.
The Confirmation screen shows the customer reference number, approver, approval time and that the welcome email was sent; the Onboarding Officer gives the reference to the customer.

requirements.statement: As an Onboarding Officer, I need to search existing customers by postcode and surname before I create a record, so that I do not create a duplicate customer.
requirements.rationale: Duplicate prevention is the stated purpose of the first screen.
requirements.source_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search, and it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

requirements.statement: The Customer Search screen shows each matching customer as one row with Customer ID, Name, Date of birth, Postcode, Account type and Status.
requirements.rationale: Column list taken from the results table on the frame; the expert did not name the columns.
requirements.source_quote: it lists anyone we already have

requirements.statement: The system saves Customer Details only when First name, Last name, Date of birth, Account type and Postcode are all filled in.
requirements.rationale: The five fields carry a * on screen and the legend reads 'fields marked * are required'.
requirements.source_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

requirements.statement: The system rejects a Customer Details save when Postcode is not in a valid UK postcode format.
requirements.rationale: Hint under the field on screen: 'UK postcode format, e.g. SW1A 1AA'. The exact rule is not stated.
requirements.source_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

requirements.statement: The system saves Customer Details when Address line 1, Address line 2, Town / City, Email address and Phone number are all empty.
requirements.rationale: The expert names the address lines and town as optional; Email address and Phone number carry no * on screen.
requirements.source_quote: The address lines and the town are optional.

requirements.statement: The Account type dropdown on Customer Details offers the options Personal and Business.
requirements.rationale: Both values also appear in the Account type column of the Customer Search results.
requirements.source_quote: Account type is a dropdown, personal or business

requirements.statement: The system records marketing consent as Yes only when the Onboarding Officer has ticked 'Customer has given marketing consent'.
requirements.rationale: The checkbox is unticked on the frame and Review & Submit shows 'Marketing consent: No'. The business rule is that the officer ticks it only when the customer has said yes.
requirements.source_quote: the marketing consent box only gets ticked if the customer actually said yes

requirements.statement: As an Onboarding Officer, I need to upload an image of the customer's ID document with its Document type, so that proof of identity is attached to the customer record.
requirements.rationale: The Documents screen has a Choose File control, a Document type dropdown and an Upload button.
requirements.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

requirements.statement: The system accepts an ID document upload only when the file is a PDF, JPG or PNG.
requirements.rationale: Taken from the hint under the file control ('PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB'); the expert did not say it.
requirements.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

requirements.statement: The system accepts an ID document upload only when the file is 10 MB or smaller.
requirements.rationale: Taken from the hint under the file control ('PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB'); the expert did not say it.
requirements.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

requirements.statement: The system shows an uploaded document with status Pending check until the document has been checked.
requirements.rationale: Pending check (amber) is visible in the Uploaded documents table on the frame.
requirements.source_quote: The status column shows pending until the document has been checked.

requirements.statement: The system changes the status of an uploaded document to Verified once the document has been checked.
requirements.rationale: Verified (green) is visible in the Uploaded documents table. Who checks the document, and where, is unknown.
requirements.source_quote: Someone checks them, I'm honestly not sure who, it just changes to verified at some point.

requirements.statement: The Documents screen lists each uploaded document with File, Document type, Uploaded date and time, Uploaded by and Status.
requirements.rationale: Column list taken from the Uploaded documents table on the frame; the expert only mentioned the status column.
requirements.source_quote: The status column shows pending until the document has been checked.

requirements.statement: The Review & Submit screen shows a read-only summary of Name, Date of birth, Email address, Phone number, Address, Account type, Marketing consent and ID document with its check status.
requirements.rationale: All eight items are visible on the frame.
requirements.source_quote: Review and Submit is a summary of everything so far. You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

requirements.statement: The system locks the customer record against editing once the Onboarding Officer has pressed Submit for approval.
requirements.rationale: Also written on screen: 'After submission the record is locked for editing.'
requirements.source_quote: Once you submit, the record locks and you can't edit it any more.

requirements.statement: A Team Lead can send a submitted customer record back to the Onboarding Officer for editing.
requirements.rationale: The expert was not sure and no send-back control was seen on any frame. Kept because it is the only stated way to correct a mistake after submission.
requirements.source_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

requirements.statement: The Approval Queue lists every submitted customer as one row with Reference, Customer, Submitted date and time, Submitted by, Status and Assigned to.
requirements.rationale: Column list taken from the frame. The screen subtitle says oldest first, but the rows on the frame are not in date order, so ordering is left as a question.
requirements.source_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status, and it shows who it's assigned to

requirements.statement: The system shows the Approve button in the Approval Queue only to users in the Team Lead role.
requirements.rationale: Also stated in the banner on screen: 'Team leads only. The Approve action is shown to users in the Team Lead role.'
requirements.source_quote: Only team leads can approve. The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

requirements.statement: Users outside the Team Lead role can view the Approval Queue.
requirements.rationale: The banner on screen reads 'Other users can view the queue but cannot approve', and the expert (not a team lead) sees the queue without the Approve button.
requirements.source_quote: The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

requirements.statement: When a customer is approved, the system shows a Confirmation screen with Customer reference number, Approved by, Approved on and Welcome email status.
requirements.rationale: All four items are visible on the frame. The reference number is what the Onboarding Officer gives to the customer.
requirements.source_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number. We give that reference to the customer.

requirements.statement: The system sends a welcome email to the Email address entered on Customer Details when the customer is approved.
requirements.rationale: The Confirmation screen shows 'Welcome email: Sent to eloette.lunmere@example.com'. The trigger being approval is implied by where the status appears; the expert did not say when it is sent.
requirements.source_quote: A welcome email goes out automatically to the address we entered.

questions.question: What counts as a match in Customer Search: exact surname and postcode, or partial / nearby matches? The results include postcode SW1A 1AB for a search on SW1A 1AA.
questions.why_it_matters: The matching rule decides how well duplicates are caught and what a developer has to build.
questions.context_quote: it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

questions.question: Must both Postcode and Surname be filled in to search, or can either be left blank?
questions.why_it_matters: Determines search validation and whether a surname-only search is allowed.
questions.context_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search

questions.question: What should happen when the officer presses Open on an existing customer, and can a customer with status Closed be onboarded again?
questions.why_it_matters: The Open button and the Closed status were seen but never explained; the team needs to know what path an existing or closed customer follows.
questions.context_quote: it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

questions.question: What exactly is the UK postcode validation rule (accepted patterns, spaces, upper/lower case) and what error message is shown when it fails?
questions.why_it_matters: A developer cannot implement 'valid UK format' without the precise rule and the failure behaviour.
questions.context_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

questions.question: Are there validation rules on Date of birth (DD/MM/YYYY only, no future dates, minimum age), Email address and Phone number, and what does the officer see when a mandatory field is empty?
questions.why_it_matters: Only the postcode rule was described; the other fields may also reject bad input, and the empty-field behaviour was not shown.
questions.context_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

questions.question: Does Save and continue create a saved customer record at that point, and can an officer leave and come back to a half-finished onboarding?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether draft records exist before documents are uploaded and how they show in search.
questions.context_quote: Then you press Save and continue.

questions.question: Who checks uploaded documents and changes the status from Pending check to Verified, and is that done inside this system or elsewhere?
questions.why_it_matters: The verification step is part of the process but the expert could not say who performs it or where.
questions.context_quote: Someone checks them, I'm honestly not sure who, it just changes to verified at some point.

questions.question: What are the full options in the Document type dropdown, and is a proof of address document required as well as the ID document?
questions.why_it_matters: Passport and Proof of address were seen and driving licence was mentioned; the table lists two documents but the form is labelled 'Upload ID document'.
questions.context_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

questions.question: What happens when an upload is the wrong file type or over 10 MB, and can an uploaded document be removed or replaced?
questions.why_it_matters: The limit is shown on screen but no error or delete behaviour was seen.
questions.context_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

questions.question: Can a record be submitted for approval, and approved, while its ID document is still Pending check? The record on screen was submitted with the ID still pending.
questions.why_it_matters: If verification must come first, both Submit for approval and Approve need a gate on document status.
questions.context_quote: You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

questions.question: How does a submitted record get sent back for editing, who can do it, and does that unlock the record and return it to the officer?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert was unsure and no send-back or reject control was seen; without it a mistake after submission cannot be corrected.
questions.context_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

questions.question: How is a submitted customer assigned to a team lead, and what does Unassigned mean for who picks it up?
questions.why_it_matters: The assignment rule affects who sees which work; one row on screen is Unassigned.
questions.context_quote: it shows who it's assigned to, though I've never worked out how it picks the person.

questions.question: Can a team lead reject a record from the Approval Queue, and are there statuses other than Awaiting approval and Approved?
questions.why_it_matters: Only an Approve action was seen; the team needs the full set of outcomes and statuses.

questions.question: Which users can view the Approval Queue, and do they see all officers' submissions or only their own?

questions.context_quote: The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

questions.question: In what order should the Approval Queue list its rows? The screen says oldest first, but the rows on the frame are not in date order (the Approved row dated 08/09/2026 is last).
questions.why_it_matters: The stated order and the shown order disagree; the team needs one rule, for example by status then by submitted date.
questions.context_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status

questions.question: How is the customer reference number (format NW-2026-31365) generated, and how does it relate to the Customer ID (format C-625922) shown in search results?

questions.question: What does Print confirmation produce, and where does Start another customer take the officer?
questions.why_it_matters: Both buttons are on the Confirmation screen but neither was pressed or described.
questions.context_quote: We give that reference to the customer.
